methodology_note: Unlike Audits 01-05's original read-only passes, every runtime-behavior finding in this audit was empirically verified against a real, live PostgreSQL instance (pgvector/pgvector:pg16, migrated to head via Alembic) in this session, not inferred from reading code alone.

findings.location: ~17 model classes' created_at/updated_at/started_at/etc. columns; live crash site backend/app/api/registry.py:129
findings.finding: Migrations declare most timestamp columns as sa.DateTime(timezone=True) (real TIMESTAMPTZ), but the ORM model declares the same columns as bare Mapped[datetime] with no explicit timezone=True, since Base has no custom type_annotation_map. SQLAlchemy uses its own (wrong, naive) Python-side type to build SQL casts on write, causing a real crash whenever application code assigns a timezone-aware datetime.now(timezone.utc) to one of these fields via the ORM.
findings.evidence: Empirically reproduced via a live test against real Postgres: writing datetime.now(timezone.utc) to Agent.last_computed_at and committing raises asyncpg.exceptions.DataError with SQL showing `UPDATE agents SET last_computed_at=$1::TIMESTAMP WITHOUT TIME ZONE`. Confirmed live and reachable: calling GET /api/agents/planner/metrics via a real TestClient against the live DB crashes with the identical error every single call -- no try/except catches it (registry.py:127-130).
findings.production_impact: GET /api/agents/{name}/metrics returns an unhandled 500 on every call in any real deployment with a live database. This is the 4th confirmed instance of a bug class PROJECT.md documents 3 prior instances of (repo.py:157, repository.py:250,273 already carry .replace(tzinfo=None) workarounds for the same root cause) -- the root cause itself (missing DateTime(timezone=True) on the ORM models) was never fixed, so more instances remain structurally possible anywhere else a bare Mapped[datetime] field is assigned an aware datetime through the ORM.
findings.confidence: High -- reproduced empirically twice (direct ORM write test, and a real endpoint call), not inferred.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit DateTime(timezone=True) to every affected Mapped[datetime] column in db/models.py, matching the real migration DDL. This is the root-cause fix; existing .replace(tzinfo=None) call sites become redundant-but-harmless, and registry.py:129 stops crashing without a separate fix.

findings.finding: save_artifact_async() correctly branches on settings.artifact_backend and uploads to S3 when configured (real, non-stub implementation, confirmed: gzip compression, correct key scheme). get_artifact() -- the only function backing the retrieval endpoint -- unconditionally reads from local disk with zero branch on artifact_backend, and never calls s3_store.load_artifact_s3().
findings.evidence: store.py:169-175 (get_artifact, local-disk-only, no backend check); artifacts.py:36-41 (endpoint calls only get_artifact, no S3 fallback); s3_store.py:87-100 (load_artifact_s3 exists, real, and is never called from anywhere in the retrieval path -- confirmed via grep, zero call sites).
findings.production_impact: Any deployment with ARTIFACT_BACKEND=s3 can save artifacts (they really land in S3) but can never retrieve them through the API -- GET /api/artifacts/{artifact_id} always 404s for every S3-backed artifact, permanently.
findings.recommendation: Branch get_artifact() (or its caller) on artifact_backend the same way save_artifact_async() does; call load_artifact_s3() when appropriate. Needs task_id/artifact_type to build the S3 key -- look these up from the artifacts DB row by artifact_id first.

findings.finding: `pnpm --filter @gridiron/web run lint || true` -- identical anti-pattern to the pip-audit `|| true` already fixed this session (Audit 05, SEC-05-019) in the same file. The trailing || true makes this step always exit 0 regardless of what ESLint finds.
findings.evidence: ci.yml:113, exact line read directly. Explains why the 2 real ESLint warnings found and fixed this session (review/page.tsx unused state, epics/page.tsx unused import) only ever surfaced as informational annotations, never as a failing check.
findings.production_impact: The frontend lint gate cannot ever fail the build regardless of severity or count of findings -- defeats the check's purpose entirely, same as the pip-audit gap did before its fix.
findings.recommendation: Remove || true, matching the precedent already set for pip-audit in this same file.

findings.finding: 4 of 6 services declare build: context: ./backend or ./apps/web, but no Dockerfile exists anywhere in the repository (confirmed via exhaustive case-insensitive search). Only db/redis (published images) would actually start.
findings.evidence: docker-compose.yml full read; Glob for **/Dockerfile* across the whole repo returns zero results; case-insensitive find in backend/ and apps/web/ also zero. Root .env.example:10-13 documents `docker compose up -d` as the project's own Quick Start step 1.
findings.production_impact: The documented Quick Start workflow has never worked for anything beyond the DB and Redis containers -- migrate/backend/worker/frontend all fail immediately with a Dockerfile-not-found error.
findings.recommendation: Add real Dockerfiles for backend/ and apps/web/ matching Procfile's real entrypoints, or update the root .env.example's Quick Start instructions to stop promising a docker compose workflow that doesn't work.

findings.location: system_settings.updated_at, chat_messages.created_at, task_images.created_at, and 019/022's archived_at columns + their justifying comments
findings.finding: 3 columns break from the dominant sa.DateTime(timezone=True) pattern with plain naive sa.DateTime(). Migrations 019 and 022 add 3 more naive columns, justified by a comment claiming 'every other timestamp column in this schema...has no explicit type' -- this claim is false; the majority of columns explicitly declare timezone=True.
findings.evidence: Direct read of all 5 migration files; cross-checked against the dominant pattern in migrations 001-007/011-016 (all explicitly timezone=True).
findings.production_impact: None currently live-crashing -- app/services/retention.py (the writer for the 019/022 archived_at columns) correctly strips tzinfo before writing. This is a documentation-accuracy and schema-consistency finding, not a live-crash finding like INFRA-06-001.
findings.recommendation: Correct the false comments in migrations 019/022. Consider a follow-up migration converting all 5 naive columns to timezone=True for full consistency if the schema hasn't shipped to a real production DB yet.

findings.finding: Uses `npm install`/`npm run dev` for apps/web instead of pnpm -- the exact npm-vs-pnpm bug class docs/DEPLOYMENT.md documents as already found and fixed in vercel.json, but run.sh (the project's other documented one-command startup path) was never updated.
findings.evidence: run.sh:74-79; DEPLOYMENT.md:79-82 documents apps/web has no package-lock.json of its own (pnpm workspace only); vercel.json and ci.yml both correctly use pnpm, confirming run.sh is the one path that regressed or was missed.
findings.production_impact: A fresh clone running ./run.sh (the documented one-command startup) gets a degraded/inconsistent npm-based node_modules layout for a pnpm workspace, inconsistent with every other entrypoint in the project.
findings.recommendation: Change to `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `pnpm --filter @gridiron/web run dev`, matching vercel.json/ci.yml.
